votes.motion: Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that SB 11 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-SB11.aiSummary: The bill creates a legal defense for some people prosecuted in Texas who were victims of human trafficking or forced prostitution. It would apply when force, fraud, or coercion led them to do the act, and the person must meet set conditions to use the defense. It takes effect 91 days after the last day of the legislative session and applies only to offenses committed on or after that date.

TX-2025892-HB25.title: Relating to a pharmacist's authority to dispense ivermectin without a prescription.

actions.text: Statement(s) of vote recorded in Journal
Reason for vote recorded in Journal
Comte report filed with Committee Coordinator

TX-2025892-HB25.policyArea: HEALTH & HUMAN SERVICES COMMISSION (V0177), Health Care Providers (I0387), Health--General (I0385)

votes.motion: Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that HB 25 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-HB25.aiSummary: The bill lets pharmacists give out ivermectin without a prescription if they follow state pharmacy board rules and any needed instructions for proper use. It also gives pharmacists protection from civil, criminal, and professional discipline when they act reasonably and follow the law. The Texas State Board of Pharmacy may adopt rules to carry it out. It takes effect on the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

votes.motion: Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that HB 16 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-HB16.aiSummary: The law changes how parts of Texas courts work, including court duties, clerk jobs, record rules, and some case priorities. It creates or changes several judicial districts and district courts in counties such as Fort Bend, Harris, Montgomery, Brazoria, Rockwall, Ellis, Comal, and others, and it also changes some district attorney offices. Some parts take effect on dates from December 1, 2025, through January 1, 2029, and the law also allows some fees and raises one criminal penalty.

TX-2025892-SR2.title: Creating the General Investigating Committee on the July 2025 Flooding Events.

actions.text: Received by the Secretary of the Senate

TX-2025892-SR2.aiSummary: The resolution creates a Senate committee to look into the July 2025 flooding events. The committee would have five senators, appointed by the Senate president, and it would review what happened around July 4, 2025. It would operate under Senate rules and state law for such committees.
